content.text:
Checked — this isn't a bug in your grid, it's two different Figma sources disagreeing with each other.

`ZimmProductCardContent`'s own recipe (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`) has its own, independently-confirmed citations from the *real, reusable* Figma component (not the "Recently Viewed" mockup):
- Image: 432px tall at 288px wide (2:3 ratio) — not 440px. The "Recently Viewed" frame's image area is a rough placeholder rectangle, not an instance of the actual "Image Group" component, so its 440px is a slightly different (and less authoritative) number.
- Content block: `paddingTop: 32px` (desktop) — and **no `paddingBottom` at all**. The recipe only documents a top padding citation; there's no bottom-padding value anywhere in it. So the card's total height is however tall its content naturally is (padding-top + name row + price, plus more rows for variations that have them) — not a fixed box padded out to some total.

Put together: 542px (33.875rem) is specifically the "Recently Viewed" *mockup's* number — a static placeholder frame, not a measurement of the real card component. The actual `ZimmProductCard` was built and documented against its own separate Figma citations, which don't add up to a fixed 542px for any variation, including the minimal `home` one (image+name+price only, closest match to the Recently Viewed card).

On top of that real discrepancy, two things in my demo specifically add height beyond even that:
1. Every grid cell has my own instance-label caption ("Default (PLP)", "Wishlist", etc.) stacked above the card — that's demo scaffolding, not part of the real component.
2. The `plp`/`wishlist` instances render more than the Recently-Viewed card ever shows (add-to-bag button, size chips, colour/size line) — those are correctly taller, not broken.

I haven't touched `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` — it's a Tier-3 shared component with its own established recipe/tests, and the "no bottom padding" gap looks like it predates this session, not something introduced here. ## ✅ UPDATE 2026-09-02 (later) — Figma nodes received; gate re-scored

Marcel supplied ~83 node URLs. All resolved (80 live, **3 dead**). Net effect: **7 🔴 → 4 🔴**,
and **SFCC-236 is now unblocked**.

### Blocker #1 — CLEARED for SFCC-236 and SFCC-83

`40000223:2822` **`Product card / Product-card`** is a single component set, **20 variants**:

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| `Size` | Desktop (288w) · Mobile (179w) · Hero (288w) |
| `State` | Default · Hover |
| `Type` | Home · **PLP/PDP** · Wishlist · `Defualt` *(sic, Hero only)* |
| `Unavailable/coming soon` | False · True |

Maps onto the ACs cleanly. Figma merges PLP and PDP into one `Type`; SFCC-236's
"Recently Viewed Full History" variation states *"same behavior as PLP card"*, so it is
`Type=PLP/PDP` — **there is no fifth variant to design.**

The rail is `40000587:38471` **`Recently Viewed / Recently Viewed`**, 3 sizes:
Desktop **1440** (5 cards @288, exact fit) · Tablet **768** (3 @256 visible, 2 hidden) ·
Mobile **402** (2 @201 visible, 3 hidden).

### Blocker #3 — RESOLVED BY THE DESIGN. It is a bag icon.

`Card-content Size=Desktop` (`40002109:26906`) contains, at
`Content > Frame > Product name and attributes > Product name and icons > Icons > touchContainer`:

```
<instance id="40002109:26891" name="Icon_bag" x="4" y="4" width="16" height="16" />
```

**`Icon_bag`, not a wishlist heart.** The `atom/add-to-wishlist` set (`40000214:6159`) exists on the
documentation board but is **not placed inside any card variant**. Figma therefore agrees with
**SPR-14/SPR-15** (amended wishlist→cart) and **contradicts CRM-113–119**.

Downgraded 🔴 → 🟡: the build direction is unambiguous (build the bag icon); what remains is
housekeeping — someone should strike the CRM rows so the next reader isn't misled.

Also confirmed in the same subtree: `Size Selector` is `hidden="true"` in the default state and
reveals on hover — matching the AC exactly. `Attributes` (Colour + Size text) and `Price` and a
`Link` atom are all present in the shared Card-content, with per-`Type` visibility set on the instance.

### Blocker #2 — CORRECTED, and narrower than first reported

Verified 04.72 (408944644) directly. Its ownership rule: *"Each component is owned by the earliest
epic in the sequence where it appears… if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage,
all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP."* **PDP's design scope lists
"product card"; PDP components-finalised = Aug 13 (Sprint 3), passed.** Search & Recommendations
(lists "recently viewed carousels") = **Aug 24, passed**. The Sep 7 dates are PLP-template /
homepage-template scope, not the card.

The one survivor: the Wishlist row separately lists **"wishlist product card"** at **Sep 21**, which
contradicts the same page's ownership rule. 🔴 → 🟡, wishlist variant only.

### Also verified directly (both drop out)

- **SPR-05** (model/item view toggle) is **struck through**: *"as per new designs - this FR is no
  longer relevant. CC: @Dani Rivett"*. Finding about the undefined toggle interaction is void.
- **SPR-16** reads *"~~clickable~~ product badges"* — display-only confirmed; no conflict with the card.

### New findings from the actual designs

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| **No Tablet variant of the Product-card exists** — only Desktop/Mobile/Hero. But the rail's Tablet (768) variant uses **256-wide** cards, which is neither 288 nor 179. Card internals at 256 are a stretched instance, undesigned. | 🟡 |
| **The 768–1022 band is confirmed empty.** Artboards exist at 402, 768, 1440. Tablet sits *exactly* on 768 — the boundary, not inside the band — and the next is 1440, so **769–1439 is unspecified**. Chakra's `md` is 768, so the one tablet artboard lands on a breakpoint edge. | 🟡 |
| **`Hero` size / `Type=Defualt`** — a fourth type covered by no AC, with a **misspelled variant value** and **two byte-identical variants** (`40004599:89265`, `40004638:120484`), which Figma treats as a variant conflict. | 🟡 |
| **`.base-size-selector` (`40003038:125876`) has a leading dot** — Figma's convention for a private/unpublished component. Won't appear in instance-swap for consuming files. | 🟡 |
| **Mobile has no Hover variant** (12 Desktop / 6 Mobile / 2 Hero). Correct for touch, and consistent with the AC — recorded so it isn't later read as a gap. | 🔵 |
| **No loading state and no empty state** anywhere in the set. `Card heading Type=Message` is the nearest thing. | 🟡 |
| **Hover is an expand, not a restyle** — heights grow (Home 489→522, PLP/PDP 522→541, Wishlist 546→565; with unavailable=True, Home 489→**570**). Budget for reflow, not a colour swap. | 🔵 |
| **The AC says "arrows appear to click through product images"; Figma ships `Slide indicator`** (`40002536:7957`, 13 variants, Qty images 5\|8) — a **dot/bar indicator**, not arrows. | 🟡 |
| **The rail's hidden cards are stale**, not a deliberate overflow depiction — 200×472.04 vs visible 201×299.82 / 256×381.85; never resized when the visible ones were. Scroll intent is an inference. | 🟡 |
| **Touch target is exactly 24×24** (`touchContainer`). Meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 minimum with zero margin. AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA. | 🔵 |
| **3 dead node links** supplied: `40004756:477`, `40004756:479` (File A), `8641:2` (File B). | 🔵 |
| **Naming hazards for any automation**: `Image Group ` (trailing space), `Products  Module Desktop` (double space), File B's only page named `-----`, its divider frame named `-`. | 🔵 |

### SFCC-84 — still 🔴, and the design is weaker than the others

The only page frame anywhere is **File B `3332:35655` "Recently Viewed", 1440×3335** — confirmed as
the See-Full-History page by its `PLP Bar desktop` containing text layers literally named
`Recently Viewed Text` and `Full History Text`. But:
- It is in the **legacy** `Zimmermann_Designs` file, which Marcel flagged **PENDING CONFIRMATION FROM DESIGNER**.
- It is **desktop-only** — no mobile, no tablet page frame exists.
- Its grid is a static **4×4 of `Products  Module Desktop` @288** — not the rail, and not a paginated grid.
- Its `Sidebar` frame is **misnamed** (holds the product grid + footer, no sidebar), and it contains

content.content:
PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports
`{Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}`, so an override without that named export breaks PLP at import time.

`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names). No design values, so it
was originally co-located with the organism (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`).

**Corrected 2026-09-04 (postbuild Round 3, commit `0f35e0c`):** that co-location was wrong for this file's
actual consumers. Unlike `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` — imported only by its one owning molecule —
this file is imported by two *sibling* molecules (`zimmProductCardMedia`, `zimmProductCardContent`), which
had to reach up into the organism's own folder to get it. Relocated to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`
directly — a genuine common ancestor, not owned by any one of the three components — and every import path
updated accordingly. `CARD_BP` was never actually added to this file in the first place; both consuming
`.css.ts` recipes import `breakpoints` from `theme/foundation` directly instead, which carries no drift
risk (single real source) but never matched this paragraph's original claim — corrected here too.

**A second file, added later in the same pattern, was found, fixed, then un-extracted entirely
(2026-09-04, Round 6) — its full history, for the record:** `organisms/zimmProductCard/productCardFixtures.ts`
(added Round 3, commit `5b49864`) held Storybook-only fixture data plus a demo wrapper component, imported
by the same two sibling molecules from the same backward direction `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was fixed
for. Its docblock cited `overrideStyling.md`'s "SFCC bridge pattern" section as justification — that
section says nothing about Storybook fixtures; the citation was fabricated (Round 4 finding). Rather than
just fix the citation and relocate it the same way (done first, commit `d0b0889`), Marcel questioned the
premise directly: unlike `zimmProductCardShared.ts` (a genuine cross-component DOM contract — a mismatch
silently breaks hover CSS), this file's contents were pure test/story sample data with no production
coupling, so duplicating it across files carries no real risk. Un-extracted entirely (commit `3814db6`) —
each piece restored locally to whichever file(s) actually use it, including a second, independently
duplicated copy of the demo wrapper in `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`, an accepted tradeoff.
**`zimmProductCardShared.ts` is the one file this reasoning still supports** — it stays at `ui-kits/` root.

**Manifest count correction:** four files exist with no citation in this section, all added mid-build and
disclosed only in their own commit messages: `zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts`, `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts`,
`zimmSlideIndicator.css.test.ts` (dedicated recipe unit tests, beyond the four-file template above), and
`organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` (a per-Figma-node coverage folder). None cross a
tier or CODEOWNERS owner — all resolve to the same `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` line as everything else in
`ui-kits/`.

**Superseded 2026-09-05 (commit `02a3203`):** `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`, cited above, no longer
exists. Marcel asked for the two separate Storybook surfaces (this file's own curated stories plus that
folder's 12 per-Figma-node stories) to become one consolidated collection organized by real product
variant/state rather than Figma node ID — every one of the 12 node-coverage stories was confirmed to be a
finer-grained decomposition of a state the main file already demonstrated via manual hover/resize, not
distinct coverage. `nodeCoverage/` was deleted wholesale (confirmed fully isolated first — only two
self-referential JSDoc mentions anywhere in the repo, no test file, no Storybook/CI config reference) and
`zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` rebuilt as the single collection: the original 8 stories kept verbatim
plus 3 new ones (`WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) closing confirmed gaps with zero prior
organism-level coverage. Net `ui-kits/`-scoped created-file count is now 28, not 29 — the manifest
correction above stands for the historical record of how the count reached 29, but 29 is no longer the
live total.

---

## 4. Architecture decisions

**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).

```
ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
  'home':     —
  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
```

`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.

The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`

I checked the ACTUAL current `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` file directly (not memory) — that's the real, audited canonical set: `plan.md`'s own build history confirms it's "8 original stories plus 3 new ones (`WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) closing confirmed gaps with zero prior organism-level coverage." My demo's 11 instances already map 1:1 onto those 11 real stories (`Default`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `HomeOutOfStock`, `Wishlist`, `WishlistOutOfStock`, `SingleImage`, `MultipleImages`, `WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) — same names, same variation/price/size-chip prop shapes. The component's real prop surface (`plp`/`home`/`wishlist` + `isUnavailable`, nothing more granular like a separate "region-unavailable") caps at exactly these 11 — there isn't a broader AC-prescribed set beyond what's already shipped.

But diffing prop-by-prop against the real file did turn up two genuine discrepancies worth fixing:

1. **Real `Default`/`Home`/`Wishlist` never pass `images`** — only `primaryImage`+`hoverImage` (the 2-image hover-swap). My `plpBase`/`homeBase`/`wishlistBase` all spread `base`, which includes the mapper's full `images` array whenever the real product has ≥2 images — meaning my "Default (PLP)" could already be rendering as a full gallery, making it visually indistinguishable from "Multiple images" instead of demonstrating the hover-swap specifically.
2. **Real `Wishlist` pre-selects a size chip** matching the item's own size (`selectedSizeChipValue: 'm'`, matching its `size: 'M'`) — mine starts with nothing selected.

Fixing both now.

content.text:
Both clean. Here's what changed and why.

**Demo now has 17 cards across 5 labeled sections**, replacing the flat 11:

| Section | Cards |
|---|---|
| **Core component** | Single image · Hover-swap pair (2 images, no gallery — new, wasn't explicit before) · Multiple images (gallery) · With sale price · Loading price |
| **PLP** | Default · Out of stock · One size |
| **Home** | Default (badge/hover-swap suppressed) · Out of stock (additive reveal) |
| **Wishlist** | Default · Out of stock · **One size — new, the one genuinely missing card** |
| **Recently Viewed (Full History)** | 4× reused PLP cards |

Each section has an on-page note explaining anything that isn't a separate buildable card — the three mobile-viewport-gated behaviors (tell you which existing card to resize the browser against instead of duplicating it), the real `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal (provable on any interactive card here, which Storybook can't do), and the Recently Viewed / Wishlist framing.

**What I did *not* add, and why** (all confirmed via the research pass, documented in the file's own updated docblock):
- **Hero variant** — orphaned Figma node, no owning ticket, no 4th `variation` value exists in the component.
- **Tablet-specific design** — no such Figma variant exists.
- **Recently Viewed *carousel*** (SFCC-83) — a different surface from the Full History grid shown here; genuinely has no code path today.
- **Three Wishlist CRM-backed states** (a distinct "What's Now" price type, a region-unavailable state, a destructive add-to-bag treatment) — PRD-confirmed but never actually built into the shipped component, so there's nothing real to demo.
- **VIC/customer-group price precedence** — explicitly deferred to SFCC-778.

One thing worth your attention, not mine to resolve here: the Wishlist section's note flags that the shipped hover-revealed size-chip picker matches PLP/Figma, but the literal Jira AC text for Wishlist only calls out image-swap + arrows on hover. That's an already-accepted design-over-AC-text call from earlier in this build, not something introduced by this demo — surfacing it since you wanted the ACs directly checkable.

input.description: Investigate mobile swipe not paging images
input.prompt:
We're on git branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component in this repo (a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront). The developer reports: "the multiple images state on mobile doesn't work on swipe — the slide indicator is there, but the swipe/gesture isn't focusing on swiping through the images." I need you to find the exact mechanism so we can plan a fix.

Background already known (don't re-derive from scratch, verify and go deeper):
- The component is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`, composed inside `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`.
- The gallery is native CSS scroll-snap: a `scrollContainer` div (`overflowX: 'auto'`, `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`, `WebkitOverflowScrolling: 'touch'`, scrollbar hidden) containing `slide` children (`flex: '0 0 100%'`, `scrollSnapAlign: 'start'`).
- The touch-only slide indicator (`ZimmSlideIndicator`, rendered when `totalSlides > 1`) is meant to track the ACTIVE slide as the user swipes — it listens for a native `scrollend` event on the scroll container and computes the nearest slide from `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` (see the `useEffect` with `handleScrollEnd` in `index.tsx`).
- Desktop hover-only prev/next arrow buttons exist in the same component; a separate always-on keyboard handler (`onKeyDown` on the scroll container, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) also calls `goToRelativeSlide`, which calls `scrollTo({left, behavior:'smooth'})` on the container.
- The developer's report is specific: the indicator dot UI is visibly present (so `totalSlides > 1` is true and images did load), but the actual touch swipe gesture doesn't scroll/page through the images at all on a real mobile device.

What to actually investigate and report:
1. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` in FULL and its `.css.ts` in FULL if you haven't already.
2. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` and its `.css.ts` in FULL — specifically looking for anything on an ANCESTOR of the media component's scroll container that could block/override touch scrolling: `overflow: hidden`, `touchAction` set to anything other than the default (e.g. `pan-y`/`none`), `pointer-events: none` inherited oddly, a `position: absolute`/`fixed` overlay sitting on top of the scroll container intercepting touch-start (check the `badge`/`close`/`carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` overlay parts' z-index/positioning relative to the scroll container — do any of them, even though visually small, have a stacking/sizing bug that puts an invisible hit-area over the whole image where swipes would start?), or any `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` handler anywhere in the ancestor chain that calls `preventDefault()` and could suppress the native touch-scroll gesture.
3. Specifically check: does the `slide`'s own hover-swap or any other CSS use `transform`/`will-change` in a way that could create a new stacking/scroll context that breaks the parent's scroll-snap? Does `scrollContainer` have an explicit `height`/`width`, or could it be collapsing to 0 real scrollable width on a real device despite working in Storybook/desktop dev (Storybook's own iframe or a specific dev-server viewport-emulation quirk could mask a real-device-only bug)?
4. Check whether `touchAction` (CSS `touch-action`) is set ANYWHERE in this component family or a shared/global stylesheet (`overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`, any `.scss` file, any base Chakra recipe this composes) to a value that would block horizontal panning specifically (e.g. `touch-action: pan-y` or `none` applied to the container or an ancestor) — this is one of the most common real causes of "scroll-snap works with mouse-drag/desktop but not with a real finger swipe."
5. Check git log/blame on `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` and `index.tsx` for when the scroll container's styles were last touched, and whether any commit message suggests this was tested only via Storybook/desktop browser resize rather than a real touch device or Playwright mobile project.
6. Check `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (if it exists) and any Playwright specs under `e2e/tests/zimm/` referencing this component for touch/swipe coverage — was a real touch gesture ever actually simulated/tested (Playwright's mobile-chrome project + `page.touchscreen` or similar), or only keyboard/click paths?
7. Also check the ORGANISM recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal mechanism mentioned in its own docblock (point 6) — could that same mechanism, or a related recent change to it, have introduced a `pointer-events` or `touch-action` side effect that affects the media child even though it's conceptually about hover/focus, not touch? Check for any recent commit changing this file.

Report back: the exact current CSS/DOM mechanism (file + line numbers) governing touch scroll on this component, whether `touch-action` is set anywhere relevant and to what, any ancestor `overflow`/positioning/pointer-events finding that could block the gesture, and your best-supported theory (or theories, ranked) for why a real touch swipe doesn't page the gallery despite the indicator rendering. Do not propose a fix yet — this is investigation only, feeding into a plan. Be thorough and cite exact file:line locations for everything you assert.
